From: Laura Chang <laura.chang@fintechco.com>

Subject: Infra compatibility gap analysis: private deploy vs hyperscaler — initial asks

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciate the walkthrough of Redwood Dedicated and the private deployment options. A few quick items the security and infra teams asked me to surface while we consolidate an internal comparison against our hyperscaler vendor (BigCloud):

- Can you confirm the minimum network egress breakout requirements for a private deployment when the control plane is customer-managed? We need a clear list of FQDNs/ports and whether TLS mutual auth is mandatory.
- For air-gapped POCs: does Redwood support a one-way outbound-only telemetry relay or is a two-way control channel required for model versioning and health checks?
- We saw the streaming demo — can you share expected latency delta (p99) when serving the same model from Redwood Private (on-prem GPU pool) vs Redwood Hosted in us-west region and vs BigCloud endpoints? A ballpark helps our SRE cost model.

Also attaching a short topology sketch we're using as a baseline. We'll stand up a lab next week and want to schedule a technical sync with your infra team.

Attachments: topology-sketch.png (image), initial-poc-scope.docx (doc)

—Laura
Principal Infra PM, FintechCo
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Infra compatibility gap analysis: private deploy vs hyperscaler — initial asks

Laura — thanks for the detailed list and for sending the sketch. Looping in Ben (solutions) and Karthik (networking/ops) to own the technical runbook. Quick responses inline, and below I propose concrete next tests for the lab.

1) Egress & Port list
- For Private with customer-managed control plane (our common VPC model) we require outbound TLS to the control plane endpoints on 443. Optional telemetry can be pushed to an outbound-only relay. Required DNS: controlplane.redwood.cloud, metrics.redwood.cloud, updates.redwood.cloud.
- If customers operate an air-gapped installation with no outbound, we ship a static bundle for model versions and a restoreable control plane image; in that configuration we do not require mutual TLS to our hosted endpoints.

2) Air-gap feasibility
- One-way telemetry relay is supported for monitoring only (push metrics). Model rollouts require either a batched bundle sync or a physical transfer if zero outbound is mandated. We'll document the exact bundle format in the POC checklist.

3) Latency delta
- Ballpark p99: Redwood Hosted (us-west) -> 40–80ms p99 for short contexts; Redwood Private (on-prem, comparable GPU pool) -> +10–30ms additional p99 depending on network (vSwitch vs direct attach). BigCloud endpoints — depends on their config (we've seen 50–150ms p99 for comparable setups). We'll run an apples-to-apples benchmark in the lab and share a readout.

Proposed lab tests (what we'll run next week):
- Networking matrix: validate outbound whitelist + route fallthroughs (test cases for DNS failures, proxy egress, NAT timeouts).
- Control plane sync: test bundle delivery, verify model integrity hashes, and simulate forced rollback.
- Air-gap scenario: simulate no-outbound and run local-only inference for 24 hours.
- Performance baseline: 1) local Private with KV cache warm, 2) Hosted us-west, 3) BigCloud endpoint (if they provide test creds) — measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost.

I've attached a draft networking matrix for the lab and a short POC checklist. Ben/Karthik — can you confirm availability for a 60-minute lab kickoff Wednesday 8/26 or Thursday 8/27?

Attachments: networking_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 38KB), redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (pdf, 24KB)

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Laura / Monica — jumping in from BigCloud ops. Happy to provide test endpoints and a short config we use for private gateway egress. A couple clarifications from our side:

- If you're planning to test network fallthroughs, we'll need a small pcap from your lab to reproduce NAT timeouts (unless Redwood can simulate). I'm attaching a sanitized pcap sample from a recent lab run — it should help your SREs craft reproducible cases.
- For mutual TLS: we require client certs only on our gateway; we can run a mode without mTLS for test purposes but can't support long-term without cert rotation automation.

If that helps, we can stand up a temporary sandbox endpoint with a read-only token for the performance comparison. Let me know the IP ranges your lab will egress from and we'll whitelist.

Meeting notes summary:
- Redwood supports both outbound-only telemetry and an air-gapped bundle workflow. Air-gapped POCs will use a signed model bundle; we will provide an integrity hash list for verification.
- Control plane options: 1) customer-managed control plane with outbound to our endpoints, 2) fully air-gapped control plane with periodic bundle imports.
- Preliminary latency expectation: Hosted (us-west) lowest p99; Private adds additional network delta depending on local topology. Exact numbers pending lab run.
